items.note: Article (17.01.2020) says the council decided on 17 Dec 2019 by majority: 1.50 EUR/h now, 2.10 EUR/h from 2020, 3 EUR/h from 2022 at parking meters; city says it serves climate goals and is part of the 30-point climate action plan. Draft source_title matches the HTML <title> tag; the visible headline differs ('Ab 2020 werden Parkgebühren in Heidelberg drastisch erhöht – werden Bus und Bahn dadurch günstiger?'). Date 2019-12 fits the decision.

Groundbreaking on 16 Jan 2020 (page dated 22.01.2020); Stadtwerke Heidelberg Garagen; 672 car and 750 bicycle spaces; opening planned for Q2 2021; initially 20 charging stations (22 kW), expandable to 120. Planned figures are kept as plans.

Article (02.11.2022) says P19 in Campbell Barracks (Nina-Simone-Str. 6, Rohrbach) opened with free parking 28-30 Oct 2022; 365 spaces; operated by Stadtwerke Heidelberg Garagen (owner Hans-Jörg Kraus); Free Flow camera number-plate recognition, no barriers; 230 kW PV on the roof; six charging stations.

Article (24.07.2023): 228 public charging points reported in December (2022); city works with Stadtwerke Heidelberg on a 500x500 m grid, ~110 squares in inhabited areas, aims to cover 80% of squares by 2025 (a target, kept as such). 'about 80 percent' is slightly looser than the page's '80 Prozent'.

Council on 15 Dec 2022 (large majority) kept the fee at 120 EUR for 2023, 36 EUR for Heidelberg-Pass holders. But the page does not say the administration had proposed 240 EUR; it says a further rise to 240 EUR 'as originally planned' was not recommended by the administration, citing economic uncertainty and the energy price crisis.
items.corrected_text: The council decided on 15 December 2022 to keep the residents' permit fee at 120 euros a year for 2023, with Heidelberg-Pass holders paying 36 euros; the administration said a further rise to 240 euros, as originally planned, was not advisable given economic uncertainty and the energy price crisis.

items.note: Press release 10.07.2023: BVerwG ruling of 13 June 2023 concerned Freiburg's fee bylaw; administration proposes repealing the bylaw and interim fee of 36 EUR for all applicants (from 120) until a legal ordinance can be issued; council to decide 20 July 2023. Kept as a proposal.
Article (18.12.2023): fee 120 EUR from 1 Jan 2024; Heidelberg-Pass(+) holders pay 36 EUR own share, city covers the rest; council decided unanimously on 14 December (2023).

Council voted by majority on 1 Feb 2024 for the revised concept and agreed to continue pursuing 'currently 17 envisaged' bollard locations to restrict entry to the pedestrian zone; extension to Theaterstraße and Neckarstaden (between Pfaffengasse and Steingasse) requires a planned separate partial-dedication procedure. The page says 'Poller' only; 'retractable' is not stated.
items.corrected_text: On 1 February 2024 the council approved a revised Altstadt traffic-management and calming concept, agreeing to keep pursuing a plan for currently 17 envisaged bollard locations to restrict vehicle entry to the pedestrian zone; extending the zone to Theaterstraße and part of Neckarstaden is planned through a separate procedure.

items.note: Press release 02.08.2024: parken.heidelberg.de shows forecast free spaces at arrival time; sorting/filters include gas-vehicle access, 24-hour opening, EV charging, baby changing, accessible WC, clearance height, price; HCC, Europaplatz and similar new garages to be integrated soon. The page has a '24 hours open' attribute, not a general opening-hours filter.
items.corrected_text: The city added features to its online parking guidance portal (parken.heidelberg.de), including a forecast of free spaces at the user's arrival time and filters such as EV charging, 24-hour opening and clearance height; new garages such as those at the HCC and Europaplatz were to be integrated soon.

items.note: Page (16.09.2024): two-level underground garage for ~1,600 bicycles and ~750 cars; garage with 162 public car spaces opened 13 Sept 2024, operated by Stadtwerke Heidelberg Garagen GmbH. Page gives exactly 162, not 'about 162' (harmless).
parking.net (13 Jan 2025): Q-Park took over a centrally located facility in Heidelberg on 1 January 2025 (not named); licence-plate recognition, ticketless, Q-Park app.

Page (22.01.2025) counts 22 'Ladesäulen' (charging stations/spaces), 10 run by Stadtwerke and 12 by private providers, and confusingly also says drivers can charge at 'seven Ladepunkte'; it does not state 22 charging points, nor explicitly 'public'. City intends to build more charging stations as part of parking management planned for 2025.
items.corrected_text: The city reported 22 EV charging stations in the Bahnstadt, 10 operated by Stadtwerke Heidelberg and 12 by private providers, and said it intended to add more as part of the parking management planned for 2025.

items.note: Page (16.10.2025): from 23 June 2025, as part of the first public-transport savings package within the city budget, bus 32 discontinued and tram 24 reduced in evenings/weekends; city says remaining lines can currently handle demand.
Press release (06.06.2025): overnight tax of 3.50 EUR per person per night from 1 October 2025; more than 1.8 million overnight stays in 2024.

Schwäbische (17.05.2026): parking meters 3 EUR/hour, also in the centre; first hour 2.50 EUR in Stadtwerke Garagen GmbH car parks. The 'increase decided at end of 2025' sentence follows directly after the residents' permit fee (120 EUR) and refers to those fees, not on-street charges; the draft wording leaves it ambiguous (and the draft's gaps list misreads it as an on-street increase).
items.corrected_text: A May 2026 overview reported on-street parking at 3 euros per hour, including in the centre, and 2.50 euros for the first hour in Stadtwerke Garagen car parks; it said the residents' permit fee was 120 euros a year and that the council had decided a fee increase at the end of 2025 which the administration was still implementing.

items.note: Undated page. It says under the current ordinance the 2026 fee is 120 EUR (digital) / 135 EUR (in person), rising to 125/140 from 1 Jan 2027 and 130/145 from 1 Jan 2028; visitor-card blocks 15 EUR for blocks 1-5, 35 EUR from block 6. '1 July 2026' on the page refers only to visitor cards becoming available online, not to the permit fee taking effect; the page does not say when the visitor-card prices started ('now' unsupported). Date 2026-07-01 is too specific.
items.corrected_text: Under the current ordinance, a residents' permit costs 120 euros in 2026 when applied for or renewed digitally and 135 euros in person, rising to 125/140 euros from 1 January 2027 and 130/145 euros from 1 January 2028; visitor-card blocks cost 15 euros each for the first five and 35 euros from the sixth.

corrected_summary: In December 2019 Heidelberg's council approved staged on-street parking charge increases to 3 euros per hour from 2022, and the residents' permit fee was kept at 120 euros in 2023, temporarily proposed to fall to 36 euros after a 2023 federal court ruling, set at 120 euros again from 2024 and scheduled to rise in steps to 2028. Stadtwerke Heidelberg Garagen broke ground on Parkhaus hip in 2020, operates the barrier-free P19 garage at Campbell Barracks opened in 2022 and the Europaplatz garage opened in 2024, and in July 2025 the council approved round-the-clock paid parking in the Bahnstadt. Other dated changes include upgrades to the online parking guidance portal in 2024, bus and tram service cuts from June 2025 and an overnight tax from October 2025.
